subject: Order Form SLA: maintenance policy, uptime target, and credits
messages:
From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@globex.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Singh <bob.singh@globex.com>, contracts@globex.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form SLA questions — uptime & maintenance

Hannah —

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form. Procurement and our cloud reliability team skimmed the SLA and have three items they need clarified before we loop Legal: uptime target, scheduled maintenance exclusions, and the service credit formula. High level: Globex needs a commitment suitable for production customer-facing workloads. Specific asks below so your legal/ops folks can respond:

1) Uptime target: we are asking for a 99.95% monthly uptime for the dedicated environment in the Order Form, with measurement by region (us-east-1). Please confirm if Redwood will commit or propose an alternative.

2) Scheduled maintenance: want a maximum of 2 hours/month (or 24 hours/year) for platform maintenance that can lead to reduced availability. Any maintenance outside that should require 30 days notice and approval for major windows.

3) Service credits: we expect a simple formula tied to % monthly downtime (e.g., X% credit per 0.1% below the target) and a cap not lower than 50% of the monthly committed fee. Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a 50% cap.

Also need an explicit severity 1 (production down) response time (acknowledge within 15 minutes, mitigation plan within 2 hours) and an escalation path with names/roles.

We attached the redlines our GC would like to start from once we have Redwood's operations positions. Happy to jump on a short call this week.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Sr. Director, Cloud Procurement
Globex Corporation

Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses inline:

1) Uptime target: We can commit to 99.95% for Dedicated capacity on a per-region basis as an optional premium SLA (this would be reflected in the Order Form as a line item). For Hosted plans our standard is 99.9%.

2) Scheduled maintenance: 2 hours/month is tighter than our current ops baseline. Ops will propose a controlled maintenance policy with a preferred default of up to 4 hours/month, but we can offer a 2 hours/month cap for Dedicated with an exception path (e.g., emergency maintenance with notice and a make-good credit).

3) Service credits: Redwood typically calculates credits in tiers (small percentage per 0.1% below SLO) and caps credits at 50% of monthly fees for Dedicated — so that aligns. Need Legal to mark the exact percentages and measurement windows.

Severity/SIRT: we can commit to 15-minute acknowledgement for Sev1 and a 2-hour mitigation plan for Dedicated customers. Will include named escalation roles in the Order Form appendix.

I've looped Marcus (Product ops) and Monica (Enterprise Sales) — Marcus, can you attach the ops redline and proposed maintenance language? Monica, can you keep Procurement in the loop on pricing impact for the 99.95 SLA?

I can do a 30-min call Wed 11am PT if that helps.

Best,
Hannah

Alice / team —

Attaching the ops-oriented redline (see attachment) and pasting the key proposed clauses so legal can vet wording quickly. These are engineered to be measurable and minimize ambiguity.

--- excerpt (proposed):
SLA: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated capacity in the specified region. Uptime measured against total elapsed time in the billing month, excluding scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and customer-caused outages."

Maintenance: "Scheduled maintenance windows for Dedicated capacity will not exceed 2 hours per calendar month. Redwood will provide at least 7 days' advance notice for routine maintenance and 30 days' notice for maintenance classified as major. Emergency maintenance required to remediate security vulnerabilities may be performed with 24-hour notice and will be documented in the monthly availability report."

Service Credits: "If monthly uptime for the region falls below the SLA, customer is eligible for the following credit tiers applied to the monthly fee for the affected capacity: 99.95% - 99.0% = 10% credit; 99.0% - 98.0% = 25% credit; <98.0% = 50% credit (cap 50%). Credits issued as a percentage of the monthly committed fee; not refundable; excludes pass-through charges."

Sev1 Response / Escalation: "Initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes; a mitigation plan within 2 hours; ongoing updates every hour until mitigation. Escalation contacts: Platform On-call, Escalation Engineer, Head of Dedicated Ops (contact details in appendix)."

---

Notes: the 2-hour monthly maintenance cap is a concession for dedicated customers only; for hosted customers the default remains 4 hours/month. The credit tiers above are intentionally simple so procurement can model costs.

Marcus / Hannah —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications before we hand this to GC:

• Uptime: Globex prefers 99.95% measured by published region metrics (we run customer-facing APIs). Can Redwood confirm instrumentation (CloudWatch or equivalent) and an independent measurement method? We need a way to dispute and validate metrics.

• Maintenance: 7 days notice for routine maintenance is OK; emergency maintenance with 24 hours' notice is not acceptable for our compliance team unless it is an absolute emergency. We need emergency maintenance to be documented and for GC to approve the workaround. Can we change emergency to "as soon as practicable with notification" and require post-event RCA and an audit trail?

• Credits: the tiering is readable, but we need the calculation example inserted in the Order Form (worked example showing credits for 0.5% downtime in a 30-day month) and require the cap be 50% — that's a hard requirement. Also want a separate audit right to request monthly availability reports and raw metric data under NDA.

If you can accept the instrumentation + audit right + sample calculation the GC will likely proceed to redline.

If it helps, I can have procurement and reliability on a 30-min call Thursday at 10am PT.

Alice

Alice / team —

Thanks — Legal reviewed Marcus's ops language and proposed the attached MSA redline with edits to reduce ambiguity. Highlights of our changes and the compromise positions we recommend for insertion into the Order Form:

1) Measurement and instrumentation: we propose that Redwood publish monthly availability reports for the region with underlying metrics exported to an agreed-upon monitoring endpoint (we suggest using a mutually accessible S3 bucket via signed access under NDA) for any disputed months. The measurement methodology will reference standard telemetry (Redwood's region-level availability metric computed from request success rates and platform heartbeat signals).

2) Maintenance / emergency: we revised emergency maintenance language to require "reasonable efforts" to provide notice; for non-routine emergency maintenance Redwood will provide a post-event RCA within 5 business days and will include a documented risk assessment. For anything requiring more than 4 hours of unplanned disruption, Customer may request a one-time credit (per incident) subject to review.

3) Service credit mechanics: legal translated the tiered approach into precise math and included a sample calculation in the appendix. We accept the 50% cap for Dedicated capacity. We added an audit right: Customer may request monthly availability logs for the preceding 6 months under NDA; Redwood will supply within 10 business days of request.

4) Escalation and response: we kept the operational commit to 15-minute acknowledgement and a 2-hour mitigation plan for Sev1. We added a directory appendix that includes named roles and a routing matrix (on-call -> escalation engineer -> Head of Dedicated Ops).

Next steps: if Globex accepts the instrumentation option (S3 logs under NDA) and the 50% cap, Legal will finalize redline and we can push to DocuSign. We have attached Redwood_MSA_redline_20270325.docx and a sample OrderForm with the SLA addendum.

I'll be available on Thu 10am PT for the call if you confirm.

Regards,
